data.long_meaning: From the Greek 'Karizomai', meaning 'to dearly love, to cherish'. In the Bible, Carissa is not a direct name, but the name is associated with Mary, the mother of Jesus. The name Carissa carries the meaning “Beloved, dear” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Carissa usually hope their child will grow to embody beloved, dear and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of deep love and devotion.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Carissa total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Carissa is popular in the Christian world. It has a rich and unique origin, derived from the Greek words 'Karizomai', meaning 'to dearly love, to cherish'. This name is a beautiful reminder of the devoted love and selflessness that God shows towards his children and that parents have towards their children. The name Carissa evokes qualities of compassion, care, and deep love.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Carissa is significant because it reflects the selfless love and care that God has shown towards humanity through giving us His Son, Jesus Christ. The name Carissa is also associated with the Blessed Virgin Mary, who is the embodiment of motherly love and devotion towards her Son. The name serves as a reminder of the more excellent way of love (1 Corinthians 12:31) that we, as Christians, should strive to live out in our own lives. It is a call to cherish and love others as God has loved us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Carissa: Beloved, Dearly Loved One. Derived from the Latin word 'carissus' meaning dear or precious, Carissa embodies the essence of being loved and cherished by the divine.

biblical_reference.note: not directly mentioned in the Bible

historical_references.reference: Carissa of mauretania, also known as Saint Carissa, was a Berber princess who converted to Christianity and dedicated her life to helping the poor and sick in the 4th century. She was martyred during the Roman persecution of Christians.

Carissa of the Thebaid, also known as Saint Carisso or Saint Karissa, was a desert mother and ascetic who lived in Egypt in the 4th and 5th centuries. She is known for her ascetic practices, spiritual teachings, and her role as a mother superior of a community of female ascetics.
historical_references.time_period: Early Christian Era, 4th and 5th Centuries AD
